t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style. Light-weight sans-serif headline on a deep navy block at top left. Below, a strict modular grid of square-cornered tiles in a checkerboard of deep navy and limestone, a few left empty as colour rhythm. Each tile carries a huge light numeral with a slash, a small-caps label, a large monospace value with unit and a hairline rule above a short note for <CONTENT>. One tile is filled with a white isometric blueprint line drawing on steel blue. Thin steel-blue frame around the grid. Flat, no shadows.
signature_idea: Design parameters set as a Swiss checkerboard of numbered tiles, with one blueprint tile breaking the grid like a photo in a poster.
strengths: each parameter is a scannable tile: label, figure, basis
very close to the brand: navy/limestone, light headline, mono values, square corners
blueprint tile gives equipment context without clutter
maps cleanly to a token-only CSS grid component
weaknesses: empty filler blocks waste space and may read as missing content on smaller screens
checkerboard of contrasting tiles is busy for seven items
invented specific values (budget, 316L) would be mistaken for real figures
logo red maple leaf and nav are off-system
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone blocks, one steel-blue accent, light Geist-like headline, mono figures, square corners and blueprint isometric line art are the brand book almost verbatim.
